texts.NIV84: The words of the Teacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem:
texts.KJV: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
texts.NKJV: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
texts.DRB: The words of Ecclesiastes, the son of David, king of Jerusalem.

texts.NIV84: "Meaningless! Meaningless!" says the Teacher. "Utterly meaningless! Everything is meaningless."
texts.KJV: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.
texts.NKJV:
“Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher;
“Vanity of vanities, all is vanity.”
texts.DRB: Vanity of vanities, said Ecclesiastes vanity of vanities, and all is vanity.

texts.NIV84: What does man gain from all his labor at which he toils under the sun?
texts.KJV: What profit hath a man of all his labour which he taketh under the sun?
texts.NKJV:
What profit has a man from all his labor
In which he toils under the sun?
texts.DRB: What hath a man more of all his labour, that he taketh under the sun?

texts.NIV84: Generations come and generations go, but the earth remains forever.
texts.KJV: One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.
texts.NKJV:
One generation passes away, and another generation comes;
But the earth abides forever.
texts.DRB: One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh: but the earth standeth for ever.

texts.NIV84: The sun rises and the sun sets, and hurries back to where it rises.
texts.KJV: The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he arose.
texts.NKJV:
The sun also rises, and the sun goes down,
And hastens to the place where it arose.
texts.DRB: The sun riseth, and goeth down, and returneth to his place: and there rising again,

texts.NIV84: The wind blows to the south and turns to the north; round and round it goes, ever returning on its course.
texts.KJV: The wind goeth toward the south, and turneth about unto the north; it whirleth about continually, and the wind returneth again according to his circuits.
texts.NKJV:
The wind goes toward the south,
And turns around to the north;
The wind whirls about continually,
And comes again on its circuit.
texts.DRB: Maketh his round by the south, and turneth again to the north: the spirit goeth forward surveying all places round about, and returneth to his circuits.

texts.NIV84: All streams flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full. To the place the streams come from, there they return again.
texts.KJV: All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea is not full; unto the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return again.
texts.NKJV:
All the rivers run into the sea,
Yet the sea is not full;
To the place from which the rivers come,
There they return again.
texts.DRB: All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea doth not overflow: unto the place from whence the rivers come, they return, to flow again.

texts.NIV84: All things are wearisome, more than one can say. The eye never has enough of seeing, nor the ear its fill of hearing.
texts.KJV: All things are full of labour; man cannot utter it: the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
texts.NKJV:
All things are full of labor;
Man cannot express it.
The eye is not satisfied with seeing,
Nor the ear filled with hearing.
texts.DRB: All things are hard: man cannot explain them by word. The eye is not filled with seeing, neither is the ear filled with hearing.

texts.NIV84: What has been will be again, what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.
texts.KJV: The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.
texts.NKJV:
That which has been is what will be,
That which is done is what will be done,
And there is nothing new under the sun.
texts.DRB: What is it that hath been? the same thing that shall be. What is it that hath been done? the same that shall be done.

texts.NIV84: Is there anything of which one can say, "Look! This is something new"? It was here already, long ago; it was here before our time.
texts.KJV: Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? it hath been already of old time, which was before us.
texts.NKJV:
Is there anything of which it may be said,
“See, this is new”?
It has already been in ancient times before us.
texts.DRB: Nothing under the sun is new, neither is any man able to say: Behold this is new: for it hath already gone before in the ages that were before us.

texts.NIV84: There is no remembrance of men of old, and even those who are yet to come will not be remembered by those who follow.
texts.KJV: There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.
texts.NKJV:
There is no remembrance of former things,
Nor will there be any remembrance of things that are to come
By those who will come after.
texts.DRB: There is no remembrance of former things: nor indeed of those things which hereafter are to come, shall there be any remembrance with them that shall be in the latter end.

texts.NIV84: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
texts.KJV: I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
texts.NKJV: I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
texts.DRB: I Ecclesiastes was king over Israel in Jerusalem,

texts.NIV84: I devoted myself to study and to explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven. What a heavy burden God has laid on men!
texts.KJV: And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all things that are done under heaven: this sore travail hath God given to the sons of man to be exercised therewith.
texts.NKJV: And I set my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under heaven; this burdensome task God has given to the sons of man, by which they may be exercised.
texts.DRB: And I proposed in my mind to seek and search out wisely concerning all things that are done under the sun. This painful occupation hath God given to the children of men, to be exercised therein.

texts.NIV84: I have seen all the things that are done under the sun; all of them are meaningless, a chasing after the wind.
texts.KJV: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all is vanity and vexation of spirit.
texts.NKJV: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and indeed, all is vanity and grasping for the wind.
texts.DRB: I have seen all things that are done under the sun, and behold all is vanity, and vexation of spirit.

texts.NIV84: What is twisted cannot be straightened; what is lacking cannot be counted.
texts.KJV: That which is crooked cannot be made straight: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.
texts.NKJV:
What is crooked cannot be made straight,
And what is lacking cannot be numbered.
texts.DRB: The perverse are hard to be corrected, and the number of fools is infinite.

texts.NIV84: I thought to myself, "Look, I have grown and increased in wisdom more than anyone who has ruled over Jerusalem before me; I have experienced much of wisdom and knowledge."
texts.KJV: I communed with mine own heart, saying, Lo, I am come to great estate, and have gotten more wisdom than all they that have been before me in Jerusalem: yea, my heart had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.
texts.NKJV: I communed with my heart, saying, “Look, I have attained greatness, and have gained more wisdom than all who were before me in Jerusalem. My heart has understood great wisdom and knowledge.”
texts.DRB: I have spoken in my heart, saying: Behold I am become great, and have gone beyond all in wisdom, that were before me in Jerusalem: and my mind hath contemplated many things wisely, and I have learned.

texts.NIV84: Then I applied myself to the understanding of wisdom, and also of madness and folly, but I learned that this, too, is a chasing after the wind.
texts.KJV: And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.
texts.NKJV: And I set my heart to know wisdom and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also is grasping for the wind.
texts.DRB: And I have given my heart to know prudence, and learning, and errors, and folly: and I have perceived that in these also there was labour, and vexation of spirit,

texts.NIV84: For with much wisdom comes much sorrow; the more knowledge, the more grief.
texts.KJV: For in much wisdom is much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.
texts.NKJV:
For in much wisdom is much grief,
And he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
texts.DRB: Because In much wisdom there is much indignation: and he that addeth knowledge, addeth also labour.
